result.summary: This PR adds a new CI job that runs macOS arm64 test_bitcoin and test_bitcoin-qt binaries, which are currently cross-built via depends but never executed, on native macOS hardware. It splits the macOS-cross-to-arm64 build out of the existing CI matrix into its own job so the new native-test job does not have to wait on the full matrix, and adds cache options (enable-cross-os-archive, enable-cross-arch-archive) to share the built binaries between the Linux cross-build job and the macOS native-test job.
result.problem: Cross-built macOS binaries are currently produced but never run, so regressions like test_bitcoin-qt segfaulting when built via depends (issue #35771) go undetected until reported by users or downstream. This affects anyone relying on the macOS release-style builds passing CI as a signal of correctness.

result.card: This PR adds a native macOS arm64 CI job to run test_bitcoin and test_bitcoin-qt binaries that are currently cross-built via depends but never executed, splitting the build out of the CI matrix and using cache sharing to pass binaries between jobs. It fixes a real gap: cross-built macOS binaries have silently broken before, as shown by linked issue #35771 where test_bitcoin-qt segfaulted undetected. fanquake gave a substantive concept ACK comparing this to existing native testing of Windows cross-built binaries, and maflcko's design questions (cache vs artifact, frozen-commit pinning) were resolved without objection. The PR was rebased on 2026-09-11 onto #35838 per fanquake's request and appears ready for review now. No open concerns remain.
